repairAndWhy.TypeScript: Reach for the property directly, so the value keeps the object it came from and a naked local still means this scope created it. Allowed only when the local is read inside a hook dependency array.
repairAndWhy.Swift: It is read once, and nothing runs between its declaration and that read. Write `{{reach}}` where `{{name}}` is read and delete the declaration, so the value keeps the object it came from and a naked local still means this scope made it.
repairAndWhy.Go: It is read once, and nothing that could change the field runs between its declaration and that read, so the reach reads the same field. Through a nil pointer the reach panics where `{{name}}` is read rather than where it was declared. Write `{{reach}}` where `{{name}}` is read and delete the declaration, so the value keeps the struct it came from and a naked local still means this scope made it.
